cases.title: Self-hosted LLM inference at scale with per-team quotas

defects: Failover path is drawn as PAI-EAS -> NAT -> Model Studio, but fallback is a gateway policy: the edge should be AI Gateway -> Model Studio (NAT only if the gateway egress requires it); as drawn it implies the EAS service calls the fallback itself.
No mention of GPU availability constraints in Singapore (A10/T4/V100/P100; A100/H100 never offered internationally), which matters for sizing a 'large Qwen model' for 2,000 concurrent users.
Autoscaling / router or prefill-decode separation is not described in the why text of the PAI-EAS node, which the guidance expects for this scale.
reasons: Covers the core ask: AI Gateway for per-team quotas and failover, PAI-EAS for self-hosted Qwen, Model Studio fallback, SLS logging, all in Singapore.
Placement follows the rules: SLS and Model Studio outside the VPC, multi-zone as single nodes, no DNS hop, no needless Auto Scaling node.
Narration states assumptions as chips and asks at most two design-changing questions with quick replies.

cases.title: EU-only training data and large distributed training (no Lingjun in Frankfurt)

defects: Lingjun node placed in Frankfurt region although Lingjun is not available in Frankfurt (only Singapore internationally).
Narration fails to state that Lingjun is not offered in Frankfurt and proposes it as the training backbone anyway.
No alternative GPU path (general PAI-DLC quota, GPU ECS or ACK) offered for the Frankfurt-only constraint.
Lingjun is allowlist/subscription-only, making it a poor default recommendation without flagging this to the user.
reasons: Lingjun is not offered in Frankfurt (Singapore is its only international region), so placing a Lingjun cluster in Frankfurt violates the EU-only data residency requirement and the catalog facts.
The design should use PAI-DLC on general GPU resources (or GPU ECS/ACK) in Frankfurt instead of Lingjun; the answer never tells the user Lingjun is unavailable there.
Otherwise the structure (DSW, DLC, CPFS, OSS, EAS, NAT, SLS all in Frankfurt) matches the expected pattern and the German narration is clear.

未提及 EAS 专用资源组/网关的计费与 scale-to-zero 限制等运维要点

cases.title: Sandbox fleet for agentic RL rollouts (international, no official reference)

defects: Model Studio is drawn as the policy inference path during rollouts, but RL rollouts typically need the current policy weights served on PAI-EAS; hosted Model Studio cannot serve the evolving policy, so the sandbox->llm edge is questionable for training rollouts
No PAI-EAS node for final policy serving, which the strong-answer guidance expects
Does not mention confirming Singapore public GPU capacity (A10/T4/V100) or browser/desktop sandbox type availability in console
reasons: Correctly uses PAI-DLC + Agent Sandbox (Flash, Singapore) with OSS/SLS, and states plainly there is no official reference, pointing to the ACK+VeRL walkthrough
Draws first on stated assumptions and asks at most two design-changing questions with quick replies
Avoids China-only PAI-Instant Service and does not make Lingjun a prerequisite

cases.title: Asked to build on PAI-LangStudio

defects: Omits the required disclosure that PAI-LangStudio retires on 2027-03-09 and that its named successor (Model Studio application development) is not open to new international accounts.
Narration wording 'isn't in the catalog' misrepresents why LangStudio is not used, instead of explaining the retirement to the user who asked for it by name.
Dify node drawn as a separate hop behind ACK (alb -> ack -> dify) double-counts the same workload; Dify runs on ACK, so a single node or containment would be cleaner.
No ingestion path shown from OSS documents into Milvus (embedding pipeline), leaving the RAG data flow incomplete.
reasons: Sound Dify-on-ACK RAG design with correct placement and multi-zone, but it never discloses that LangStudio retires 2027-03-09 or that Model Studio's successor app builder is closed to new international accounts.
Narration says 'PAI-LangStudio isn't in the catalog', which is evasive rather than explaining the retirement and successor situation the user needs to hear.
Good assumptions-as-chips and two relevant quick-reply questions; diagram structure, edges and regional placement are clean.
